newsitem.title: UK: Pizza Express shares dip after bid denial.
newsitem.headline: Pizza Express shares dip after bid denial.

text.p: Shares in restaurant operator Pizza Express Plc dipped on Monday, after a report in the Financial Times dousing bid hopes that have boosted the stock in recent sessions.
Yet dealers said the decline was modest set against the sharp gains of recent sessions and said there were signs of institutional buying of Pizza Express shares.
They pointed out that a bid could still arrive at some stage regardless of the company's denial of having received a bid approach.
"What the company is saying is fair enough but there are other buyers out there," said one market-maker, "there are plenty of people who want a slice."
The stock was down 15p at 752-1/2 by 1402 GMT in volume of 521,789 shares, after on Friday leaping 57p.
From a level below 140p in April 1995, Pizza Express shares rocketed to a record 824p last Friday -- some 56 percent higher than its level at the end of 1996.
The FT quoted chief executive David Page saying that no-one had approached the company about a takeover in the four-and-a-half years since its flotation.
Page said the company's high stock market rating would probably deter other companies from bidding, attributing its strong rise to the company's expansion plans.
The FT said Pizza Express planned to open an additional 30 restaurants in the next 12 months.
The pub and restaurant sector has been boosted by a series of major acquisitions in recent months, such as Whitbread Plc's 133 million stg purchase of Pelican Group last year.
